t: Which of the following statement is incorrect about electromagnetic waves?
s: An accelerating charge produces an oscillating electric field. This oscillating electric field creates an oscillating magnetic field. This oscillating magnetic field then creates another oscillating electric field. This cycle of oscillating electric and magnetic fields keeps regenerating each other, producing EM waves and as electromagnetic (EM) waves, composed of oscillating electric and magnetic fields, do not transport electric charge themselves. They carry energy and momentum, but not charge. Electromagnetic (EM) waves do not travel at the same speed in all media; they travel at the speed of light (approximately 3×10^∧8m/s ) only in a vacuum, and their speed decreases when passing through matter. Therefore correct answer is option 4.
o: EM waves are produced by accelerating charges.
EM waves do not transport charge.
Energy of the EM waves is shared equally between the electric and magnetic fields.
EM waves travel with the same speed in all media.

t: An electromagnetic wave of frequency 100 MHz propagates through a medium of conductivity, σ=10mho/m. The ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is [Take 1/4πε₀=9×10⁹Nm²/C²]
s:
According to Ohm’s Law in point form, the conduction current density is proportional to the electric field (E) : J_c=σE
The maximum value occurs when the electric field is at its peak ( E₀ ) : (J_c)ₘₐₓ=σE₀
Displacement current density arises from a electromagnetic wave, the electric field can be represented as E=E₀sin(ωt).
Maxwell defined displacement current density as : J_d=ε(∂E)/(∂t)
⇒J_d=ε∂/(∂t)(E₀sin(ωt))=
εωE₀cos(ωt)
The maximum value occurs when the cosine term is 1 : (J_d)ₘₐₓ=εωE₀
The ratio of the maximum values is: Ratio =((J_c)ₘₐₓ)/((J_d)ₘₐₓ)=σE₀/εωE₀=σ/εω
The conductivity ( σ ) of the medium is, σ=10mho/m
The angular frequency ( ω ) is 2πf=2π×(100×10⁶)
=2π×10⁸rad/s
Since no specific medium permittivity is given, we use the permittivity of free space ( ε₀ ). Given 1/4πε₀=9×10⁹, then ε₀=1/(36π×10⁹).
Substituting these values into the ratio: Ratio =0/(×2π×10⁸)(​₁1)/(36π×109)=(10×36π×10⁹)/(2π×10⁸)
Ratio =180×10¹=1800
Therefore, the ratio of maximum conduction current density to maximum displacement current density is 1800
